summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and migratory joint pain with rash. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction, and her symptoms were attributed to a paralytic ileus and inflammatory joint process. Workup revealed no active infection, with negative blood, stool, and joint fluid cultures. Her elevated creatinine resolved, likely due to prerenal causes, and thrombocytopenia improved spontaneously without evidence of HIT recurrence. Chronic lung changes were stable, and SVC stent patency was partially confirmed. Symptoms improved with supportive care, and she was discharged home with plans to follow up with rheumatology for pending viral and autoimmune serologies.
